newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine opposition stages telephone boycott.
newsitem.headline: Argentine opposition stages telephone boycott.

text.p: Argentina's opposition parties staged a 15-minute boycott of telephone services Monday to protest a recent rise in local call rates.
The Radical Party and center-left Frepaso alliance called on Argentines to keep their phones firmly on the hook for 15 minutes from 1245 local time (1545 GMT).

They also called on householders to bash pots and pans with spoons and on drivers to sound their car horns during the protest. Local media reported that several hundred demonstrators gathered outside the headquarters of Telefonica Argentina in Buenos Aires.
Frepaso leader Carlos Alvarez admitted that it was hard to tell how many people had boycotted their telephones.
"That will depend on what the (telephone) companies tell us, or what lies they tell us," he told the private DyN news agency.
A spokeswoman for Telecom Argentina -- which boosted rates along with Telefonica -- said that it would not be possible to assess the impact of the telephone boycott for at least a day.

The government in late January issued a decree authorizing a rise in local call rates and big cuts in charges for long-distance and international calls. A judge last Friday issued a ruling suspending the changes, but the government was expected to appeal -- allowing the companies to use the new tariff structure.

Telefonica and Telecom had waged a long lobbying campaign for the tariff changes, which they said would make charges fairer for business in the provinces. They also hoped it would make them more competitive when the Argentine phone market is thrown open to all competitors, probably in the year 2000.

But consumer groups and opposition parties fought hard against the changes and argued in public hearings ending in December last year that private users' telephone bills would rise and the companies would pocket the difference.
The telephone firms say the restructuring would not mean higher profits.
Telecom is controlled by France Telecom and Telefonica by Telefonica de Espana.
